text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- National commission in charge of follow-up of social accord signed in August last year examines ways to solve conflicts, notably lay-offs.
- Libyan Industry and Mines Minister heads delegation of businessmen on a working visit to Morocco.
- Regionalisation raises question of more funds to achieve self-reliance.
- Europe first trade partner with 64.1 percent of overall operations.
- Tourism Minister says need for structural reforms to bring three to four million tourists to Morocco by the year 2000.
- State-owned Compagnie de Navigation Maritime (COMANAV) which was in the red in 1994 is reviving following a stringent strategy to straighten out its finances.

- World Bank report says need for more contributions, higher retirement age and less generous pensions. It also advocates creating pension funds to encourage savings as foreign investments are insufficient to boost economy.
